info.title: agentes.chat operator API
info.description: Workspace and account lookups, workspace standing, the events feed and review blocks, the workspaces' computers from an external provisioner, and who may sign up (the waiting list and early-access invitations, ADR 0078), for the people who run this instance (ADR 0056).

state.description: `off` without both Turnstile keys. While `unreachable` (this server can't reach Cloudflare) or `secret_refused` (Cloudflare refuses `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`), every request goes through unchecked.

blocked.description: Networks refused in the last 10 minutes because their page couldn't load the check (`human_check_blocked`), each counted once: an IPv4 address, or an IPv6 /64. Any client can claim its page couldn't load it, so read it beside `passed`.

passed.description: Tokens Cloudflare passed in the last 10 minutes. When the widget is down for everyone, `blocked` rises while this falls. Clients claiming it is down don't move it.

testing.description: `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` is one of Cloudflare's test secrets. They refuse real tokens, and the one that passes takes a public dummy token from anyone. Right only on a test server.

OperatorBotCheck.description: The bot check before public forms (ADR 0075).

params.description: Values for the translated message (names, limits…).

next.description: `cursor` for the next page; null on the last one.

OperatorStandingState.description: `active`; `hold`: its agents stop (no model, computer, routine or invitation), people still read and write; `suspended`: the workspace refuses everything to everyone, and its runs and tasks stop at once.

lastSeenAt.description: Last time they had this workspace open.

channels.description: Channels and forums, not archived; no direct messages.

note.description: The operator's own note: never shown to the workspace.

OperatorStandingNotice.description: `shown`: the workspace is told the reason, the change goes into its audit log and a new state notifies its owners and admins. `silent`: it is told only that it is paused, and nothing is written where it can read it. Use `silent` only when an authority's order forbids telling them.

sessions.description: Its 10 newest sessions on record, newest first. Signing out deletes a session.

sessionsRevoked.description: Sessions deleted by this call (0 when unblocking).

next.description: `after` for the next call; the same value when there was nothing new, null only before any event.

type.description: `user.signed_up`, `session.created`, `user.deleted`, `organization.created`, `organization.deleted`, `invitation.created`, `agent.created`, `mail.sent`, `run.finished`, `task.finished`, `desktop_control.ended` or `content.viewed` (ADR 0056 §5 lists each one's `data`). Ignore types you don't know: new ones keep v1.

userId.description: The person the event is about or who acted.

next.description: `cursor` for the next page; null on the last one.

since.description: When this state (and step or reason) began.

requestedAt.description: When its people started waiting: the computer's last removal, else the workspace's creation.

expectedReadyAt.description: With `preparing`: the earliest ready time you gave in this wait.

OperatorProvisioning.description: What you last said about it; null: nothing yet.

OperatorMachineSpecs.description: What the workspace is told it gets.

enrollCode.description: Single use. The computer redeems it at `POST /api/machines/device/token` (`{ deviceCode }`) on the public address, like a confirmed connection code. Never log it.

managed.description: The workspace's own computer, the one you issue.

mode.description: `invite`: only people with an invitation sign up (a workspace's, or early access). `open`: anyone. Always `invite` while this server is its agents' computer (`HOST_COMPUTER_TOKEN`).

forcedOpen.description: `ALLOW_SIGNUP=true` on this server: sign-up is open whatever `mode` says.

emails.description: This server sends email, so invitations can go out.

unconfirmed.description: Entries that never confirmed their address.

waiting.description: Confirmed, with no invitation (in any state) and no account.

signedUp.description: Confirmed, whose invitation made an account.

workspaceCreated.description: Confirmed, whose invitation made its workspace.

joinedAt.description: When it joined the list (or the imported time).

confirmed.description: Entries already there, unconfirmed until now.

unchanged.description: Already confirmed, or repeated in this call.

next.description: `cursor` for the next page; null on the last one.

usedAt.description: When an account was made with it.

userId.description: That account; null once it is deleted.

workspaceCreatedAt.description: When its one workspace was made.

workspaceId.description: That workspace; null once it is deleted.

OperatorInvitationState.description: The first that holds: `revoked`, `workspace_created`, `signed_up`, `expired` (the link no longer signs anyone up), else `sent`.

get.summary: The token works and this server answers, with its bot check's state

schema.description: An org id, part of its name, or part of a member's email; any case.

parameters.description: An org id, part of its name, or part of a member's email; any case.
parameters.name: q

allOf.description: Only the workspaces in this standing.

parameters.description: Only the workspaces in this standing.
parameters.name: standing

get.summary: One workspace: its owners and admins, and how much is in it
One account: its workspaces and newest sessions

put.summary: Hold, suspend or restore a workspace
put.description: Enforced by this server where work starts: model calls, computer calls, routines, invitations and, when suspended, every permission check. Suspending also stops its runs and its tasks on computers now; cutting a computer's network is up to the operator's own controls on it. Held or suspended, it waits for no computer: what its provisioner last said goes (a ready computer stays), and it is a request again once active. It takes effect at once in this process and within 5 seconds in the server's others. Setting what is already set tells nobody again.

reason.description: Shown to the workspace with the notice `shown`, its owners' notice included. On agentes.chat Cloud, `review` reads as the automatic review hold's line, `ended` (a plan that ended) as it is, and any other reason is followed by how to contest it, so name the Terms section it rests on.

put.summary: Hold one agent, or let it go
put.description: Held, the agent starts nothing (no run, model call, computer work, routine or bridge call) and is never picked to answer; the rest of the workspace works. What it is doing stops at its next model, computer or bridge call. The workspace reads only that the agent is paused, never the reason. On agentes.chat Cloud it reads the hold's kind with how to contest it (`network` for a reason starting with `network.`, else `operator`), and the agent's responsible person and the workspace's owners and admins get a notice, replaced when it is held again for another kind and closed when the agent is let go. At once in this process, within 5 seconds in the others.

put.summary: Block an account, or let it back
put.description: Blocked: its sessions and phones are signed out now, it can't sign in again, every workspace refuses it on its next request (no waiting for a session cookie to expire) and its open connections close. Unblocking lets it sign in again; it keeps its workspaces. On agentes.chat Cloud the refused sign-in reads the block's kind, never its reason: `abuse` for `abuse.resignup`, `legal` for `legal_hold`, else `other`.

get.summary: What happened on this instance, oldest first, as metadata
get.description: Recorded only while the operator API is on, and kept 90 days. Paging never skips an event: one is served only once its transaction, and every transaction that began before it, has ended.

schema.description: `next` of the previous page; absent: from the oldest event kept (90 days). One from before the database was restored from a dump is refused (400 `stale_cursor`): start again without it and skip the event ids you already have.

parameters.description: `next` of the previous page; absent: from the oldest event kept (90 days). One from before the database was restored from a dump is refused (400 `stale_cursor`): start again without it and skip the event ids you already have.
parameters.name: after

get.summary: What one run, task or screened session did, as one redacted text block
get.description: The only content this API gives: the request, the tool calls with their results, the reply (a run), the prompt, command and output (a task), or the text a person in control of an agent's screen had on it (a session of `desktop_control.ended`, on a server with `SESSION_SCREENING`: from memory only, until 10 minutes after the segment ended, then 404). Credentials are masked and workspace text is inside `<external_data>` blocks. Every read is recorded as a `content.viewed` event first.

schema.description: Why it is read (a sample, a report, a case): kept in the `content.viewed` event.

parameters.description: Why it is read (a sample, a report, a case): kept in the `content.viewed` event.
parameters.name: reason

schema.description: Who reads it: an operator, or the service that samples.

parameters.description: Who reads it: an operator, or the service that samples.
parameters.name: operator

get.summary: Workspaces waiting for their computer, oldest first
get.description: Active workspaces whose computer isn't ready (one on hold or suspended is never listed). Empty unless `MACHINE_PROVISIONING=external`.

put.summary: Say how far the workspace's computer is
put.description: Its people see it live, with the time left and the stage. The time `since` restarts only when the state, step or reason change. One wait counts down to the earliest ready time you gave it: a later one changes nothing they see, so a part running long reads as running over, until another state, a removal or a hold starts a new wait. A ready time over a minute ahead (the wait's earliest), `waiting` or `problem` tells the owners they'll get an email when it's ready (when this server sends email). Refused (409 `provisioning.ready`) once the computer is ready, until it is removed, and (403 `org.paused`, `org.suspended`) unless the workspace is active: one held or suspended waits for no computer, and what you last said of it is gone.

state.description: `ready` is not yours to set: it comes with the computer's first hello.

step.description: With `preparing`: reserving, starting, installing or connecting; ignored otherwise.

stage.description: With `preparing`: what the computer is doing within `step` (ordering, wiping, starting, booting, updating, restarting, network, firewall, apps, connecting); ignored otherwise. Any word is kept: the apps say one they have no words for as its step.

reason.description: With `waiting`: capacity; ignored otherwise. `approval`, from an older client, reads as capacity.

expectedReadyAt.description: With `preparing`: when the computer should be ready, at most 7 days ahead; ignored otherwise. A wait counts down to the earliest time it was told: a later one, or a report without one, leaves it as it is, so people see the wait run over.

etaSeconds.description: From an older client, in place of `expectedReadyAt`: read as that many seconds from now.

post.summary: The workspace's computer, and a code for it to connect with
post.description: One per workspace: the first call makes it, every later one issues a new code for the same computer (an earlier unused code stops working), and one removed comes back. The code lives 10 minutes; once redeemed, the computer's first hello makes it ready and gives it the workspace's agents that have no computer. Refused (403 `org.paused`, `org.suspended`) unless the workspace is active.

get.summary: The workspace's computers, its own and the ones its people connected

delete.description: Before wiping or retiring it: its token and unused codes stop working, its connection closes, its agents are left with no computer, and an active workspace is a request again, waiting from now (one held or suspended waits for none). 404 when the workspace has no such managed computer (also when it was already removed).

put.summary: Open sign-up to everyone, or back to invitation only
put.description: Takes effect at once, with no restart. Setting the current mode changes nothing. On agentes.chat Cloud, while it is `invite`, an account makes a workspace only with an early-access invitation that hasn't made one yet; `open` lets every account make workspaces, each with its own computer. Refused (409 `signup.host_computer`) to open while this server is its agents' computer (`HOST_COMPUTER_TOKEN`).

409.description: This server is its agents' computer (`signup.host_computer`)

get.summary: The waiting list against the invitations
The next confirmed entries still waiting, oldest first
get.description: A read: invite exactly these (`POST /early-access/invitations`), so a retry never invites more than you saw. Skips addresses sign-up wouldn't take; they still count as waiting.

post.summary: Add confirmed addresses to the waiting list
post.description: In one transaction, up to 5000 entries, deduplicated on the address in lower case. New ones join confirmed, at `joinedAt` (a future one reads as now) or else in the list's order; an unconfirmed entry is confirmed; anything else is `unchanged`, so a repeat changes nothing. `invalid` holds the indexes of the entries that aren't addresses (sign-up's own rule), never the addresses. Imported entries are never sent to the email provider's contacts.

post.summary: Invite addresses to create an account and a workspace
post.description: Each address, up to 200, gets an email with a link to sign up with that address only, valid 14 days, in the language of its invitation, else of its waiting-list entry, else `locale`, else pt-BR. One invitation per address: inviting it again sends the same invitation a new link (the old one stops working), unless `resend` is false. Answers come in the request's order, once per address. Outcomes: `invalid_email`, `signed_up` (its invitation made an account), `has_account`, `already_invited` (with `resend: false`), `recent` (sent in the last 2 minutes, so nothing went out), `resent`, `invited`. Refused (409 `early_access.no_email`) on a server that sends no email.

get.description: `counts` count every invitation by state, whatever `state` and `q` say.

parameters.description: The first that holds: `revoked`, `workspace_created`, `signed_up`, `expired` (the link no longer signs anyone up), else `sent`.
parameters.name: state

schema.description: Any part of the address, in any case.

parameters.description: Any part of the address, in any case.
parameters.name: q

post.summary: Send an invitation again, with a new link
post.description: The old link stops working, the invitation is no longer revoked and runs 14 days from now. Within 2 minutes of the previous send nothing goes out (`sent: false`). Refused (409) once it made an account (`early_access.used`), when the address has an account (`early_access.has_account`), and on a server that sends no email (`early_access.no_email`).

409.description: Used, the address has an account, or no email (`early_access.*`)

post.description: Its link stops working, and an account it made can no longer make its workspace with it. Revoking again answers the same. Refused (409 `early_access.workspace_created`) once its workspace exists.
